slides.title: Introduction to Concepts (C++20)
slides.prompt: C++20 Concepts are compile-time predicates that constrain template arguments, yielding clearer error messages and making template requirements explicit.

slides.title: Concept Definition Keyword
slides.prompt: Fill in the keyword used to define a custom concept.
slides.codeSnippet:
template <typename T>
___ Printable = requires(T x) { std::cout << x; };

slides.title: Requires Clause Syntax Placement
slides.prompt: Which of the following demonstrates a valid placement of a requires clause?
options: template <typename T> requires std::integral<T> void process(T v);
template <typename T> void process(T v) concept std::integral<T>;
requires template <typename T> void process(T v);
template <typename T> process(T v) constraint std::integral<T>;
slides.correctAnswer: template <typename T> requires std::integral<T> void process(T v);

slides.prompt: What is a major advantage of Concepts over traditional SFINAE techniques?
